motivo: Re-chequeo contra fuentes primarias de EE. UU. La frase rechazada antes ('thick overcast vs light haze') ya no esta: la frase 6 y el caption ahora dicen solo 'clouds block some UV, thicker clouds block more, but the EPA says UV can still burn you on a cloudy day'. Esto coincide con la EPA (Guide to the UV Index: 'Cloud cover reduces UV levels, but not completely. Depending on the thickness of the cloud cover, it is possible to burn on a cloudy day, even if it does not feel warm or seem bright'; transmision: dispersas 89 %, rotas 73 %, cubierto 31 %). Las cifras de la AAD (hasta 80 %, SPF 30+, broad-spectrum, water-resistant, cada dos horas, nieve) coinciden textualmente con aad.org. Todas las afirmaciones de salud estan verificadas y atribuidas correctamente; no hay probables, dudosas ni falsas. Observacion menor, no bloqueante: el guion y el caption omiten 'or after sweating' y 'all skin not covered by clothing'; es omision, no error.

afirmaciones.texto: You skip sunscreen when it's cloudy. (gancho)
afirmaciones.fuente: No es afirmacion factica; es planteo del gancho

afirmaciones.texto: Dermatologists say that's a mistake. / Dermatologists say not so fast. (caption)
afirmaciones.fuente: AAD, https://www.aad.org/news/survey-shows-sun-protection-lacking-in-winter (recomienda protector solar tambien en dias nublados)

afirmaciones.texto: The American Academy of Dermatology says even on cloudy days, up to eighty percent of the sun's harmful UV rays can get through the clouds. (caption: up to 80 percent ... can penetrate the clouds)
afirmaciones.fuente: AAD, misma pagina: 'Even on cloudy days, up to 80 percent of the sun's harmful UV rays can penetrate the clouds.' Cifra, atribucion y 'up to' coinciden.

afirmaciones.texto: You can't feel UV. Heat and brightness aren't the same thing, so a gray sky feels safe when it isn't. (caption: You can't feel UV)
afirmaciones.fuente: EPA, https://www.epa.gov/sites/default/files/documents/uviguide.pdf y materiales SunWise: la UV no se ve ni se siente; se puede quemar 'even if it does not feel warm or seem bright'

afirmaciones.texto: Same in winter: the academy says snow reflects the sun's rays too. (caption: snow reflects the sun's rays too)
afirmaciones.fuente: AAD, misma pagina: 'It's easy to get sunburned during colder months because snow reflects the sun's damaging rays.' (EPA tambien: nieve, agua y arena reflejan UV)

afirmaciones.texto: Clouds do block some UV, and thicker clouds block more.
afirmaciones.fuente: EPA UV Index, https://www.epa.gov/sunsafety/learn-about-uv-index : transmision de UV con nubes dispersas 89 %, rotas 73 %, cubierto 31 %; NOAA CPC tambien (espesor de nube)

afirmaciones.texto: The EPA says UV can still burn you on a cloudy day. (caption: you can still burn on a cloudy day)
afirmaciones.fuente: EPA, https://www.epa.gov/sites/default/files/documents/uviguide.pdf : 'Cloud cover reduces UV levels, but not completely... it is possible to burn on a cloudy day'

afirmaciones.texto: The rule to save: SPF thirty or higher, broad-spectrum, water-resistant, and reapply every two hours. (caption: SPF 30 or higher, broad-spectrum, water-resistant, reapply every two hours)
afirmaciones.fuente: AAD, misma pagina: 'broad-spectrum, water-resistant sunscreen with an SPF of 30 or higher' y 'reapply every two hours or after sweating'. Cifras coinciden; omite 'or after sweating' (omision, no error).

afirmaciones.texto: Do you wear sunscreen on cloudy days? Yes or no? / Send this to the friend who says it's cloudy, I'm fine.
afirmaciones.fuente: Preguntas e interaccion, no afirmaciones facticas

afirmaciones.texto: Caption: Sources: American Academy of Dermatology; U.S. EPA.
afirmaciones.fuente: Ambas instituciones confirmadas arriba; la atribucion corresponde a lo que cada una dice
